issue: classifySourceLocation runs `if (extension === '.jsonl' || /ledger/i.test(fileName)) return classes.LEDGER_STATE;` before its repo-code fallback, so any source file whose name contains 'ledger' is classed as ledger state. That includes deep-research-ledger-schema.ts and check-ledger-stem-producers.cjs. This contradicts the declared contract in runtime/feature-catalog/coverage-graph/source-quality-class.md section 1, that the class comes 'from where the source lives' so a leaf cannot raise source diversity, and the only ledger-state fixture (upsert-script.vitest.ts:268,280) is a .jsonl state file. Reach: computeResearchSourceDiversityFromData (coverage-graph-signals.ts:674-688) counts distinct quality_class values per question, and convergence.cjs:447-451 makes sourceDiversity >= 1.5 a blocking STOP guard. Case: an honest research leaf studying this runtime cites only code, convergence.cjs and deep-research-ledger-schema.ts, and gets diversity 2. The guard passes when the true diversity is 1 and the guard should block. Before this diff the leaf supplied quality_class freely, so this is incomplete hardening of the new derivation, not a regression. It is still in reach, because the code now claims to derive the class. Fix: apply the ledger rule only to state files (.jsonl/.json, or a state/ledger artifact directory), not to every file name that contains 'ledger', and add a fixture showing that a code file named *ledger*.ts classes as repo-code.

The fan-in partition guard runs only when at least one lineage registry carries a frontier (hasFrontier at :875 for research and :1139 for review). When fanout-run recorded a frontier_partition but no lineage registry has a frontier, the merge returns no frontier key, no partitionGuard, no frontier_partition_guard output field and no stderr warning, although every dealt node is unreported. A registry with no frontier reaches the merge when a lineage has no registry file and the merge rebuilds one: reconstructReviewRegistryFromState (:1630) projects no frontier, and neither does reconstructResearchRegistryFromState. The case where every lineage of an expansive fan-out lands there (each died before its reducer wrote a registry) is plausible but not proven end to end, so this stays P2. Both loop protocols (deep-review loop-protocol.md:474, deep-research loop-protocol.md:419) promise the guard names any dealt node no lineage reports, and D-010-03 keeps it report-only, so the guard goes silent in exactly the case where every lineage lost its nodes. Fix: build the merged frontier whenever any lineage has one or the recorded partition holds at least one id, so an all-missing partition yields partitionGuard {passed: false, missing: [...]} and the warning. The existing no-frontier, no-partition tests stay unchanged.

issue: seedViolatesReadOnlyBoundary now removes quotedScope from the focus before it runs the mutation-verb guard (:178), on the docstring premise that the scope is path data (:35). For a frontier-unanswered seed, the scope is the node scope that a leaf proposed. frontier-admit.cjs scopeInsideReviewTarget returns true for any review target that is not a file list (:484), and fan-out binds review_target_type spec-folder by default, so for those runs the scope is unvalidated free text. A scope such as "implement the fix in src/x" passes the guard and is spliced verbatim into the seed focus, which becomes the next review focus. The template wording (Read-only review of ...) and the leaf read-only rules still apply, so this is hardening rather than a reachable write. Fix: exempt only path-shaped scope entries, such as those with no whitespace or that pass the same path test frontier-admit uses, and keep running the guard on any other scope text. The case at divergent-pivot.vitest.ts (keeps a frontier seed whose scope path happens to name a mutation verb) still passes, because its scope is a path.
